course_outline_concepts: Fixed-mix era (GLaM, PaLM) — hand-tuned weights as the baseline
DoReMi: proxy model + group DRO to learn a domain reweighting; when proxy-optimal transfers
Mix as a stage-specific lever: pretraining mix ≠ mid-training mix ≠ SFT mix
How Llama 3 / OLMo 2 set mixing weights in practice — what they report, what they hide

sources.what_to_extract: Proxy-model Group DRO minimax objective; exponentiated-gradient update on domain weights; 280M proxy → 8B transfer; 2.6× step speedup on The Pile; Pareto per-domain perplexity improvement; GLaM task-tuned comparison.

Gradient-similarity selection for targeted SFT; contrast with DSIR distribution-similarity; reusable low-rank gradient datastore; transferability across model sizes; target-set dependence as the failure mode.

What Llama 3 discloses vs hides about the pretraining mix; 15.6T tokens with capability-bucketed synthetic data; post-training mix (~50-80% synthetic rejection-sampled); per-capability pipelines imply per-capability weights.
Two-stage curriculum: OLMo-Mix-1124 (3.9T) then Dolmino cooldown (~50B); stage separation encodes a pretrain-mix vs mid-train-mix distinction; the Tulu 3 SFT mix is a third mixture.
Explicit three-stage recipe (Dolma 3 Mix ~6T pretrain, Dolmino 100B mid-train, Longmino 50B long-context) plus Dolci SFT/DPO/RLVR mixes; the public demonstration that mix is stage-specific.
Closed-mix counterpoint: 14.8T 'diverse high-quality' tokens with no domain-weight disclosure; shows what the industry default is when labs choose not to publish.
Mid-training as a distinct stage with its own mix objective; installing reusable priors; the case that mix choice at mid-training beats more RL under fixed compute.
Quality as a scaling variable; why 'the mix' is actually 'the mix times per-domain effective sample size'; two mixes with equal nominal tokens can be on different curves.
Repeat-vs-new tradeoff interacts with mix: upweighting a scarce domain is implicit repetition; the mix lever cannot be analyzed independently of the epoch count per domain.
